records.label: spacr.qt.linked_selection.LinkedSelection.unregister_object_opener#2
records.source: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed screen and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-screen guarantee above is unchanged.
records.context: Compared with ``==``, not ``is``. The pattern this module documents — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in the constructor and ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` in ``closeEvent`` — hands over a *different bound-method object* each time, because Python builds a new one on every attribute access. Under an identity check that made every withdrawal a silent no-op, so the process-wide registry kept a reference to a destroyed application view and the next ``open_objects`` reached it. Bound methods compare equal exactly when their ``__self__`` and ``__func__`` match, which is the question being asked; anything that does not define ``__eq__`` (a lambda, a ``partial``) still falls back to identity, so the two-application view guarantee above is unchanged.
records.translation: Comparaison avec ``==`` et non avec ``is``. Le modèle documenté par ce module — ``register_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` dans le constructeur et ``unregister_object_opener("annotate", self.open_object_request)`` dans ``closeEvent`` — transmet à chaque fois un *objet de méthode liée différent*, car Python en construit un nouveau à chaque accès à l’attribut. Avec un test d’identité, chaque désinscription devenait silencieusement sans effet : le registre global au processus conservait une référence vers une vue d’application détruite et le prochain appel à ``open_objects`` l’atteignait. Deux méthodes liées sont égales exactement lorsque leurs ``__self__`` et ``__func__`` correspondent, ce qui est précisément la question posée. Tout objet sans ``__eq__`` (une fonction lambda ou un ``partial``) revient encore à l’identité ; la garantie concernant deux vues d’application reste donc inchangée.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#5
records.source: **Keyset paging, not OFFSET.** Each chunk asks for ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite walk (and throw away) every skipped row, so chunk 500 of a 400 k-row table would cost 500× chunk 1 — the "fast" version would get slower the further you scrolled. Only tables with no usable key (views, composite-primary-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables) fall back to ``OFFSET``, and those are small by construction.
records.context: **Use keyset paging instead of OFFSET.** Fetch each chunk with ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` and ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` makes SQLite scan every skipped row, so chunk 500 costs about 500× as much as chunk 1 and the "fast" version gets slower. Small views and composite-key ``WITHOUT ROWID`` tables have no usable row key and use ``OFFSET`` as a fallback.
records.translation: **Utilise la pagination par jeu de clés plutôt que OFFSET.** Chaque bloc est obtenu avec ``rowid > <last rowid seen>`` et ``ORDER BY rowid``. ``LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`` oblige SQLite à parcourir toutes les lignes ignorées : le bloc 500 coûte donc environ 500× autant que le bloc 1 et la version "fast" ralentit au fil du défilement. Les petites vues et les tables ``WITHOUT ROWID`` à clé composite n’ont pas de clé de ligne utilisable et emploient ``OFFSET`` comme solution de repli.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.db_browser#14
records.source: 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` must be on — it is off by default and lives in Preferences, not on this screen. 2. The database must have been chosen explicitly in this session (``set_database(..., explicit=True)``). 3. The user must tick "Edit mode" *and* confirm; ticking alone does nothing. 4. The row must be addressable by ``rowid`` or a primary key. Without one, the edit is refused — an UPDATE matching on column values can hit many rows, which on a measurements table is silent mass corruption. The write also probes ``COUNT(*)`` for the row address first and rolls back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The typed text must be coercible to the column's declared type. SQLite will cheerfully store ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column; :func:`coerce_for_column` refuses instead.
records.context: Editing is allowed only when all five checks pass. 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` is enabled in Preferences; it is off by default and is not on this screen. 2. This session explicitly selected the database with ``set_database(..., explicit=True)``. 3. The user selected "Edit mode" *and* confirmed it; selection alone does nothing. 4. The row has ``rowid`` or a primary-key identifier. Otherwise refuse the edit: matching column values could silently update many measurement rows. Before writing, probe ``COUNT(*)`` and roll back unless ``rowcount == 1``. 5. The text converts to the declared column type. SQLite accepts ``'abc'`` in an INTEGER column, but :func:`coerce_for_column` must refuse it.
records.translation: La modification n’est permise que si les cinq contrôles réussissent. 1. :func:`spacr.qt.preferences.get_db_browser_editable` est activé dans Preferences ; il est désactivé par défaut et ne figure pas sur cette vue. 2. La base de données a été choisie explicitement dans cette session avec ``set_database(..., explicit=True)``. 3. L’utilisateur a sélectionné "Edit mode" *et* l’a confirmé ; la sélection seule ne fait rien. 4. La ligne possède ``rowid`` ou un identifiant de clé primaire. Sinon, refuse la modification : une correspondance sur les valeurs des colonnes pourrait modifier silencieusement de nombreuses lignes de mesure. Avant l’écriture, vérifie ``COUNT(*)`` et annule la transaction sauf si ``rowcount == 1``. 5. Le texte peut être converti vers le type déclaré de la colonne. SQLite accepte ``'abc'`` dans une colonne INTEGER, mais :func:`coerce_for_column` doit le refuser.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.outliers.register#2
records.source: ``SECTION_EXPLORE`` rather than ``SECTION_RESULTS``, and the reasoning is worth writing down because the first instinct is the other one. This screen looks like QC — it is about whether to believe what a run produced — but what it *does* is what the Gate Editor and the Feature Explorer do, and it sits beside them: you pick features, you move a threshold, you watch a distribution answer, and what comes out is a **column** the user then filters or gates on. Results & QC holds the screens that hand back a verdict; this one hands back a question with the evidence attached, and :meth:`~spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model.OutlierResult.filtered` is the only place a row is ever dropped and it has to be called on purpose.
records.context: ``SECTION_EXPLORE`` rather than ``SECTION_RESULTS``, and the reasoning is worth writing down because the first instinct is the other one. This application view looks like QC — it is about whether to believe what a run produced — but what it *does* is what the Data-selection boundary Editor and the Feature Explorer do, and it sits beside them: you pick features, you move a threshold, you watch a distribution answer, and what comes out is a **column** the user then filters or data-selection boundaries on. Results & QC holds the application views that hand back a verdict; this one hands back a question with the evidence attached, and :meth:`~spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model.OutlierResult.filtered` is the only place a row is ever dropped and it has to be called on purpose.
records.translation: ``SECTION_EXPLORE`` plutôt que ``SECTION_RESULTS`` ; la justification mérite d’être écrite, car le premier réflexe est l’inverse. Cette vue d’application ressemble à du QC — elle demande s’il faut croire le résultat d’une exécution — mais elle *fait* la même chose que l’éditeur de frontières de sélection de données et l’explorateur de caractéristiques, auprès desquels elle se trouve : on choisit des caractéristiques, déplace un seuil, observe la réponse d’une distribution, et le résultat est une **colonne** que l’utilisateur filtre ensuite ou soumet à des frontières de sélection. Results & QC contient les vues d’application qui rendent un verdict ; celle-ci rend une question accompagnée de ses preuves. :meth:`~spacr.qt.widgets.outlier_model.OutlierResult.filtered` est le seul endroit où une ligne est supprimée et cette méthode doit être appelée volontairement.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.power#4
records.source: **The screen computes no statistics of its own.** Every number on it comes out of :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters`; the only arithmetic here is counting how many replicates cleared the user's threshold. The translation from "genes, plates, fold-change" to simulator keyword arguments lives in one function, :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.power_design.simulator_kwargs`, so a run started here and the same run typed at a Python prompt are the same call. The test suite asserts that byte for byte on a fixed seed.
records.context: **The screen computes no statistics of its own.** Every number on it comes out of :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters`; the only arithmetic here is counting how many replicates cleared the user's threshold. The translation from "genes, plates, fold-change" to simulator keyword arguments lives in one function, :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.power_design.simulator_kwargs`, so a run started here and the same run typed at a Python prompt are the same call. The test suite asserts that byte for byte on a fixed seed.
records.translation: **La vue ne calcule aucune statistique elle-même.** Chaque nombre provient de :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters` ; le seul calcul effectué ici consiste à compter le nombre de réplicats qui franchissent le seuil de l’utilisateur. La traduction de "genes, plates, fold-change" en arguments nommés du simulateur réside dans une seule fonction, :func:`spacr.qt.widgets.power_design.simulator_kwargs`. Ainsi, une session de traitement lancée ici et la même session saisie dans une invite Python produisent le même appel. La suite de tests vérifie leur égalité octet par octet avec une graine fixe.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.project_browser#4
records.source: **A project the registry has never seen is still listed.** Projects are found by walking the disk, so a folder copied from a colleague appears the moment the browser is pointed at its parent — with its stage, its size and the date its files were last written. What it does *not* show is "0 stale", which would read as *clean*: with no provenance there is nothing to compare against, so the state column says "unknown — nothing recorded" and the note says why.
records.context: **A project the registry has never seen is still listed.** Projects are found by walking the disk, so a folder copied from a colleague appears the moment the browser is pointed at its parent — with its stage, its size and the date its files were last written. What it does *not* show is "0 stale", which would read as *clean*: with no provenance there is nothing to compare against, so the state column says "unknown — nothing recorded" and the note says why.
records.translation: **Un projet que le registre n’a jamais vu figure tout de même dans la liste.** Les projets sont découverts en parcourant le disque. Un dossier copié depuis un collègue apparaît donc dès que le navigateur vise son dossier parent, avec son étape, sa taille et la date de dernière écriture de ses fichiers. Ce qui n’apparaît *pas* est "0 stale", car cela serait interprété comme *clean* : sans provenance, aucune comparaison n’est possible. La colonne d’état affiche donc "unknown — nothing recorded" et la note en explique la raison.

records.label: spacr.qt.screens.report#1
records.source: The screen is deliberately thin. Everything it knows about a run folder it learns from :mod:`spacr.report`, which is headless, read-only and testable without Qt. This file is the part that has to be a GUI: pick a folder, say what was found and — just as loudly — what was **not**, choose a format, and write the file off the GUI thread.
records.context: The screen intentionally contains little logic. It learns about a run folder from :mod:`spacr.report`, which is headless, read-only, and testable without Qt. The GUI must choose a folder, clearly report **both present and missing results**, choose a format, and write the file outside the GUI thread.
records.translation: La vue contient volontairement peu de logique. Elle apprend tout ce qu’elle sait d’un dossier d’exécution auprès de :mod:`spacr.report`, qui fonctionne sans interface graphique, en lecture seule, et peut être testé sans Qt. La GUI doit choisir un dossier, signaler clairement **à la fois les résultats présents et ceux qui manquent**, choisir un format et écrire le fichier hors du chemin d’exécution GUI.

records.label: spacr.qt.synthetic#7
records.source: Settings CSVs are written in the two-column ``Key,Value`` format, the first of the header pairs `spacr.qt.screens.app_screen.AppScreen ._load_settings_csv` tries, so the "Import settings…" button restores every value into the form. Reading one straight from Python means naming the columns — ``load_settings(path, setting_key="Key", setting_value="Value")`` — because `spacr.utils.load_settings` *defaults* to the other spelling (``setting_key``/``setting_value``, what `spacr.io.save_settings_to_db` writes) and raises rather than guessing.
records.context: Settings CSVs are written in the two-column ``Key,Value`` format, the first of the header pairs `spacr.qt.screens.app_screen.AppScreen ._load_settings_csv` tries, so the "Import settings…" button restores every value into the form. Reading one straight from Python means naming the columns — ``load_settings(path, setting_key="Key", setting_value="Value")`` — because `spacr.utils.load_settings` *defaults* to the other spelling (``setting_key``/``setting_value``, what `spacr.io.save_settings_to_db` writes) and raises rather than guessing.
records.translation: Les fichiers CSV de réglages utilisent le format à deux colonnes ``Key,Value``, le premier couple d’en-têtes essayé par `spacr.qt.screens.app_screen.AppScreen ._load_settings_csv` ; le bouton "Import settings…" restaure donc chaque valeur dans le formulaire. Pour lire directement un tel fichier depuis Python, il faut nommer les colonnes — ``load_settings(path, setting_key="Key", setting_value="Value")`` — car `spacr.utils.load_settings` utilise *par défaut* l’autre orthographe (``setting_key``/``setting_value``, celle qu’écrit `spacr.io.save_settings_to_db`) et lève une exception au lieu de deviner.

records.translation: narration texte prononcé par le narrateur, également utilisé comme sous-titre. action fonction appelable facultative qui modifie l’UI. records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker#7
records.source: **Read-only.** Opening the picker reads column names and nothing else. The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.

The connection is ``file:…?mode=ro`` plus ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — the same pair :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` and :mod:`spacr.agreement` use — so SQLite itself refuses a write. The dialog never creates a column: it returns a *name*, and the write path that owns creation (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, which does it lazily with ``ALTER TABLE``) stays where it is.
records.translation: **Lecture seule.** L’ouverture du sélecteur lit les noms de colonnes et rien d’autre. La connexion utilise ``file:…?mode=ro`` avec ``PRAGMA query_only = ON`` — la même paire qu’emploient :mod:`spacr.qt.screens.db_browser` et :mod:`spacr.agreement` — si bien que SQLite refuse lui-même toute écriture. La boîte de dialogue ne crée jamais de colonne : elle renvoie un *nom*, tandis que le chemin d’écriture responsable de la création (``annotate_engine.ensure_annotation_column``, qui la réalise paresseusement avec ``ALTER TABLE``) reste à sa place.
